tasks.prompt: How should we model orders in the warehouse? Sources: order headers (order_id, customer_id, order_total, status, ordered_at) and line items (order_line_id, order_id, sku, qty, unit_price). Analysts want revenue and units sold. Someone proposed one fct_orders with both order_total and line_qty.
criteria: states explicit grain(s) as one row per … and refuses mixing header and line in one fact
names separate facts and shared/conformed dimensions (customer, date, product or equivalent)
includes grain tests (uniqueness, no fan-out, measure reconcile)

tasks.prompt: Customer plan (free/pro/enterprise) changes over time. Finance must attribute order revenue to the plan at order time, not the current plan. Model the customer dimension and how orders join it.
criteria: chooses SCD type 2 (or equivalent dated dimension) and rejects Type 1 overwrite for this use
specifies effective dating and a current-row flag (or equivalent)
explains how a fact joins the version of the dimension as-of the fact timestamp

tasks.prompt: Product analytics has signup, login, purchase, and refund events plus a request for a daily customer wide mart. Debate is activity schema vs Kimball stars. Advise and sketch tables.
criteria: states activity-schema grain (one row per activity occurrence) separately from any daily mart grain
refuses two grains in one table and says when a wide mart is acceptable
uses conformed entity/date keys across the chosen shapes
